help.first.title: First steps
help.first.intro: These steps take you from the start screen to a calendar file with your own meetings. They use the Scrum template; the other templates work the same way.
help.first.step.start: Open the view {control}. As long as the file has no {levelTeamLc}, it shows the start screen {title}.
help.first.step.open: Choose {control}. A short wizard asks a few questions.
help.first.step.create: Choose {control}. The new team gets the roles, cadence, categories and meetings of the template, and the person attends every meeting of the Product Owner. The calendar opens with the card {done}, which leads to the next steps.
help.first.step.team: The field {field} already holds a name, and {start} is today. Keep them or change them, then choose {control}.
help.first.step.people: Under {heading}, type a name into the field Product Owner, for example your own. Separate several names with commas.
help.first.step.frame: Under {heading}, check the time zone, the region for holidays and the planning horizon, then choose {control}.
help.first.step.meetings: Open the view {control} and check the meetings of the template: {when}, {next} and {participants}. To change a meeting, choose {edit} in its row.
help.first.step.calendar: Open the view {control}. Each day shows its meetings; choose a day to see its details.
help.first.step.load: Open the view {control}. The table {table} lists your person's meeting hours per week, and the column {fte} shows their share of the working week.
help.first.step.exchange: Open the view {control}. Under {scope}, choose {person}, then select your person in {pick}.
help.first.step.export: Choose {control} and save the .ics file. It holds the meetings of your person in the planning horizon.
help.first.next: How to add the file to Outlook, Google Calendar or Apple Calendar is explained under {ics}.
help.first.other: To look around first, choose {example} on the start screen: it opens a file with four sample teams, two of them grouped. {file} opens a Caldence file you already have.
help.areas.title: {levelAreas}
help.areas.what: {levelAreas} group several {levelTeamsLc} into one unit with its own people, hours and meetings. There is one level only: each {levelTeamLc} is in at most one {levelAreaLc}, and {levelTeamsLc} without one work as before. To create one, choose {add} in the menu {actions} at the top of the sidebar. The {team} selection then lists it with its {levelTeamsLc}.
help.areas.pages: While one of them is selected, the sidebar entry {area} has two pages. {structure} shows who works where and how many hours a week: add people with {person} and pick the member {levelTeamsLc} with {teams}. {overview} compares the cadences and the meeting load of the {levelTeamsLc} and shows the meetings {levelInArea}. Cadences are compared, not synchronised: every {levelTeamLc} keeps its own.
help.areas.drill: In {overview}, a click on a {levelTeamLc}, a meeting or a week opens the matching view. A meeting is highlighted there, not opened for editing; editing starts with the pencil. A button “← … overview” with the unit's name then leads back in one click. While presenting, picking a unit of this level from {area} or from an empty meeting list shows its {overview} right away. {how} unfolds how shares and costs are counted.
help.areas.groups: People fall into three groups, named the same everywhere: {areaOnly} (for example the lead), {both} (for example the Product Owners) and {teamOnly}.
help.areas.time: Time {levelInArea} is counted on its own, not as time {levelInTeam}. In the example, Kim works 32 h a week in Team Gamma and 4 h {levelInArea}; the PO Forum {levelInArea} is part of the 4 h and does not raise the meeting load of Team Gamma. Hours {levelInArea} are not summed up per {levelTeamLc}.
help.areas.invite: A meeting {levelInArea} can invite a role from every {levelTeamLc}: under {participants}, choose {fromTeams}. Everyone with that role in the {levelTeamsLc} of the {levelAreaLc} is invited, also in {levelTeamsLc} added later. Until you set their hours {levelInArea} in {structure}, these people have 0 h there, and the meeting shows a warning.
help.areas.names: Names of the two levels are set in {settings} under {names}, for example Bereich and Team or Platform and Product. The template {safe} creates a Release Train on the upper level, with its {levelTeamsLc}.
help.first.areas: Do you plan several {levelTeamsLc} that belong together? Read {areas} next.
help.views.title: The views
help.views.intro: Choose a view in the list of views. Above every view are the buttons for the file ({new}, {open}, {save}, {saveAs}); Calendar and Meeting load also have the filters {role} and {person}. At the top of the sidebar is the {team} selection; the button {actions} next to it holds {plan}, {addTeam}, {rename}, {duplicate} and {delete}. While there is no {levelTeamLc} yet, the Calendar shows the start screen instead, and Meeting load, Meetings & cadence and {levelTeam} offer {plan2} and {example}.
help.views.areas: When you group {levelTeamsLc} (see {areas}), the {team} selection also lists the upper level, with its {levelTeamsLc} below. While one is selected, the sidebar entry {area} holds the pages {structure} and {overview}. {calendar} and {load} then show the meetings of all its {levelTeamsLc} and its own; {role} narrows them to one role everywhere, and {person} works as before. {meetings} plans the meetings {levelInArea}, and {settings} names the two levels under {names}.
help.views.filters: The filters apply to {calendar} and {load}, which show the selected {levelTeamLc}. {role} narrows them to what one role {levelInTeam} attends. {person} shows the meetings of one person across all {levelTeamsLc}; the calendar then also marks meetings that overlap. While a person is selected, {role} cannot be changed; set {person} back to {all} to use it.
help.views.phone: On a phone, a tab bar at the bottom shows Calendar, Meeting load, Meetings and {levelTeam}. The file bar keeps {save}; {new}, {open} and {saveAs} are in the ⋯ menu ({more}) next to it, together with the other views and the links. The role and person filters share one row.
help.views.calendar: {week} shows a week, {month} a month and {range} the whole planning horizon with one row per week. In {week} and {month}, {prev} and {next} page back and forth ({prevWeek} and {nextWeek} in {week}). {today} returns to the current date, or to the start of the planning horizon when today is outside it. Each day shows its meetings in the colour of their category and marks public holidays, school holidays, the cadence and milestones. Days outside the planning horizon and non-working days are marked too.
help.views.calendar.legend: Below the month, the legend names the categories of the meetings shown; the hours at the top right of a day are its meeting hours.
help.views.day: Choose a day to open its details next to it: every meeting with its time, hours (all its people together), category, repeat rule, roles and, with several teams, its team, plus the public holiday and overlaps. {edit} opens the meeting under Meetings & cadence. When {skip} is on, meetings on a public holiday are listed as skipped. {close}, the Escape key or a click outside closes the details.
help.views.weeks: In {range}, every week of the planning horizon has one row: its Monday, its events (cadence, milestones, public holidays, school holidays and weeks with a warning), the hours of each role (all its people together) and the {total} with a bar. The current week is marked {current}. {warn} and {cadence} show only those weeks. Weeks with a warning measure each person on all their {levelTeamsLc} and {levelInArea}, as Meeting load does.
help.views.load: {role} at the top shows the typical week: the total of all people (a role without people counts as one person), the hours of every role with the average share per person and the FTE, and the peak week. {chart} shows every week of the planning horizon, with the average as a line and weeks with a warning in orange. {base} shows the hours per week of every category and role. {person} lists the members with their average meeting hours per week, their share in meetings, the room before the limit and the peak week. Each person is measured on all their {levelTeamsLc} and {levelInArea}, so they are over or under the limit in every scope alike; the column “of which {levelInTeam}” shows their part here. Meeting load counts meeting time only; other work does not count. {warnings} names, in one line per person, the weeks in which they are clearly above their usual load (a load spike) or over the limit. With an hourly rate in the settings, the {costs} card shows the cost per week, in the planning horizon and per category. {calc} explains the numbers.
help.views.meetings: The meetings {levelInTeam} and the cadence they follow. The {cadence} sits in one line at the top; {change} opens its type ({sprint}, {flow} or {pi}), length in weeks and start date. When the length changes, meetings on a cadence day in the second half keep their distance to the end, so Review and Retrospective stay at the end of the sprint; a line names the moved meetings, and Undo takes the change back. {add} opens the form for name, category, repeat rule, time, duration, preparation and the roles taking part with their share. With {scale}, the duration follows an assumption {levelInTeam}. Above {save}, {effect} shows what the change does to hours, meeting load and, with an hourly rate, cost per week and in the planning horizon; nothing is saved until {save}, and {cancel} leaves the file unchanged. On a phone the effect is one line. Every row has {edit}; {duplicate} and {delete} sit in its ⋯ menu. The headings {meeting}, {next} and {cost} sort the table, a second click reverses the order; same-day meetings follow their start time. {group} groups the rows by category with their cost per week. On a phone each meeting is a card, and a list above them sorts. Below the table are the {cycles} with the milestones that meetings can refer to, and the {categories} with their colours; categories apply to the whole file.
help.views.team: Everything about the people {levelInTeam}. Under {members} you assign a person with a role; one person can have several roles. Every member has their {hours}, the weekly hours they work {levelInTeam}. Typing a new name creates the person on the way. {assumptions} are numbers such as the team size, which scaled meeting durations use. At the bottom, folded away, are the {people} and {roles} of the whole file; every person shows where they work and for how many hours.
help.views.settings: Everything that applies to the whole file. {general} holds {language}, {region}, {timezone} and {hpw}; a new team member starts with these hours. Below are the {workdays}, the {horizon}, {skip}, the {thresholds} and, under {costs}, the {hourlyRate}: with a rate, Meetings and Meeting load show what meetings cost. The language can also be switched below the list of views; next to it you pick the appearance: light, dark or matching the system.
help.views.split: A person in several {levelTeamsLc}: when you type the name of someone who already works elsewhere under {another} or {members}, the app asks for their hours here and fills in what is left of the {hpw}. When all their hours add up to more than the {hpw}, {load} says so under their name, and so does their card under {structure}, for example “52 h – more than 40 h a week”. Click the name in {load}: a {levelTeamLc} without meetings for their role reads “0 h – no meetings for this role”.
help.views.templates: Under {builtin} you create a {levelTeamLc} from Scrum, Kanban or SAFe. You can also import a template file or export a {levelTeamLc} as a template; see {more}.
help.views.export: {export}: under {scope}, choose a {levelTeamLc}, a role or a person. Set the period with {from} and {to}, an optional {reminder}, and under {include} whether public holidays, school holidays and milestones are added. Then choose {button}.
help.views.import: {import}: choose {button} and select an .ics file. Choose the target under {team} and the roles under {roles}, then check the list of items found. Items marked {duplicate} are not selected; items Caldence cannot use are listed under {skipped} with the reason.
help.region.title: Regions and holidays
help.region.intro: The {region} decides which public holidays and school holidays Caldence knows.
help.region.import: If your region is not in the list, choose {import} and select a region file. Caldence adds the region to the file and selects it; {undo} removes it again. Imported regions are saved in the Caldence file.
help.region.remove: To remove an imported region, first select another region, then choose {remove}.
help.region.warn: If the {horizon} ends after the date until which the school holidays of the region are known, {settings} and the calendar in {weeks} show a warning. A file with an unknown region uses no holidays until you choose a region or import its region file.
help.calc.title: How the meeting load is calculated
help.calc.duration: Duration: a meeting lasts its {duration}. If {scale} is ticked, the duration is {base} + {perUnit} × the value of the chosen {assumption}, rounded up to the next multiple of the value in {grid}.
help.calc.share: Share and preparation: every role under {participants} takes its {share} of the duration; 0.5 means every other time. {prep} adds that percentage of the time on top.
help.calc.members: Members: every member with that role {levelInTeam} gets these hours.
help.calc.named: People invited by name: each person under {named} gets the hours themselves, also from another {levelTeamLc}. If one of their roles is invited too, they still count once, with the share of their own row. Costs, meeting load, the calendar export and their own filter count them like any member; templates hold no people.
help.calc.holidays: Holidays: when {skip} is on, meetings on public holidays are skipped and count no hours. School holidays do not change the meeting load.
help.calc.base: {baseTable} and the tiles in {roleTable} show the typical week of the repeat rules, independent of the planning horizon and holidays. One-off meetings and meetings relative to a milestone are not part of it. Every person in a role counts; a role without members counts as one person, as for the cost. A role’s percentage is its average per person: its hours ÷ the {hours} of its people (with a person chosen: their weekly hours). The FTE value is capacity: hours ÷ the {hpw}; with a person chosen it is left out. The chart and the people table show the average in the planning horizon instead.
help.calc.average: Average: {personTable} adds up a person's hours in every week of the planning horizon, across all their {levelTeamsLc} and {levelInArea}, and divides them by the number of weeks.
help.calc.fte: {fte}: meeting hours per week ÷ the {hours} of the person, both across all their {levelTeamsLc} and {levelInArea}, in every scope. 100 % is the whole working week. “of which {levelInTeam}” divides only the meetings {levelInTeam} by the weekly hours there. {room} is the limit × the weekly hours minus the meeting hours: room for meetings, not free working time, because other work does not count here.
help.calc.warn: {warnings}: a week is listed when a person's share in meetings is over the limit (field {maxFte}), or when they have a load spike: more than the multiple of their usual load in the field {warnFactor}. The usual load of a week is the person's average, or the hours of their recurring meetings in that week if that is more. So a peak that comes back with the cadence, such as every sprint start, is not a load spike, but a one-off meeting or a cycle milestone on top of it can be. Both values are under {thresholds} in {settings}. The limit always counts all of a person's meetings and weekly hours in all their {levelTeamsLc} and {levelInArea}, the same in every selection; this also holds for the weeks with a warning in the Calendar.
help.calc.cost: Costs: when {hourlyRate} in {settings} is filled in, Meetings and Meeting load show the {costs} card. A meeting costs its hours (with share and preparation) × the number of members in the role × the rate. A role without members counts as one person for the cost and in the Meeting load tiles and chart, but adds no hours to any person. The {costs} card and the {levelAreaLc} cost table name such roles. Per week follows the typical week, “in the planning horizon” adds up all meetings of the planning horizon without holidays. With a sprint or PI, Meetings & cadence also shows the cost per sprint or PI: the cost per week × its length in weeks; a cadence in flow shows per week only. A row with preparation names its share, e.g. “incl. 25% preparation”. Without a rate, no costs are shown.
help.calc.areas: Upper level: time {levelInArea} is counted as its own hours and does not raise the meeting load {levelInTeam}. People invited from every {levelTeamLc} have 0 h {levelInArea} until their hours are set there; until then the meeting shows a warning. Hours {levelInArea} are not summed up per {levelTeamLc}. See {areas}.
help.calc.overview: {overview} of an upper level: the share of a {levelTeamLc} is pooled over all its members, their meeting hours ÷ their weekly hours there. {teamShare} in the table counts the recurring meetings of a typical week. The weeks below count each real week: one-off meetings count, meetings skipped on holidays do not; {avg} is the average of these weeks. {loadTile} counts the recurring meetings of everyone in the {levelAreaLc}, its own meetings included.
help.calc.example: Example: a 60-minute meeting with 50 % preparation and share 1 counts 1.5 hours. For a person with 40 hours per week, 8 such meetings a week are 12 hours, or 30 % of the week in meetings.
help.where.title: Where is each value set?
help.where.caption: Where each value is edited
help.where.intro: Values for the whole file, such as the {hourlyRate}, are in {settings}. People, roles and values that belong to one {levelTeamLc}, such as its {assumptions}, are in {team}. Meetings, cadence, cycles and categories are in {meetings}.
help.templates.title: Templates
help.templates.apply: Apply: in {templates}, choose {apply} for Scrum, Kanban or SAFe, check the field {teamName} and choose {create}. The new team gets its roles, cadence, categories and meetings and becomes the selected team; {open} takes you to it. {undo} removes it again. SAFe also puts a Release Train above the team, with Release Train Engineer, Product Management and the PI events. A second SAFe team joins the same Release Train. The start screen {start} offers the same templates.
help.templates.import: Import: choose {importButton} and select a template file. Check the {preview} and the field {teamName}, then choose {create}.
help.templates.export: Export: under {exportHeading}, choose the {team}, enter a name in {name} and choose {exportButton}. You can share the file, and others can import it.
help.templates.people: A template holds no people. Add people in {teamView} and give them their roles there.
help.files.title: Files and autosave
help.files.format: Everything you plan is in one file named like plan.caldence.json. The file also remembers where you were (the {levelTeamLc} or {levelAreaLc}, and the page) and opens there again.
help.files.areas: Files of older versions open as before; they just have no upper level yet. A file in which {levelTeamsLc} are grouped needs Caldence 1.36 or newer to show everything.
help.files.buttons: {new} starts an empty file. {open} reads a file. {save} writes to the open file. {saveAs} writes a new file. If there are unsaved changes, {new} and {open} first ask whether to save them.
help.files.status: Next to the buttons you see the file name, or {untitled}, and whether there are {unsaved} or the file is {saved}.
help.files.print: {print} prints the current view or saves it as PDF, also while presenting, with its what-ifs. A line at the top names the file, the print date, the hourly rate and the planning horizon.
help.files.present: {present} shows the plan in a meeting, for example on a projector: file actions and editing step aside and the type grows. Duration, rhythm and cadence can change as what-ifs; the effect shows at once, and {reset} brings back the plan from before. {hideNames} shows people as Person 1, 2, … {stop} or Esc discards every what-if; the file stays as it was.
help.files.fallback: Browsers without file access download the file on Save and ask for it on Open.
help.files.autosave: Caldence also saves your work in this browser, so a reload brings it back. Autosave is no replacement for saving a file. If the browser does not allow it, the bar says {autosaveOff}.
help.files.privacy: Nothing is sent anywhere. Your data stays on your device.
help.install.title: Install and offline use
help.install.install: Caldence can be installed from your browser (install icon in the address bar or Add to Home Screen). After the first visit it also works offline.
help.install.update: Caldence looks for a new version every hour and whenever you return to it. When there is one, a notice says {available} {reload} saves your work in this browser and switches to the new version; {later} hides the notice.
help.ics.title: Import into your calendar
help.ics.intro: Export a .ics file in {exchange} (see {first}), then import it in your calendar app:
help.ics.areas: Under {scope}, the choice {team} also lists the upper level: its file holds only its own meetings {levelInArea}, since its {levelTeamsLc} have files of their own. With a single {levelTeamLc} chosen, the file holds only the meetings {levelInTeam}; a person's file also holds the meetings {levelInArea} they attend. {zip} makes one file for every entry of the list, so nothing is in two files.
help.ics.remember: {exchange} opens with what you last exported in this browser. If you chose {me} in the wizard, that is your own person at first. {toCalendar} in {meetings} opens with your person when you attend these meetings, otherwise with the meetings {levelInTeam}. The choice stays in this browser, not in the file you pass on. After an export, a button leads straight to these steps.

help.keys.caption: Keyboard shortcuts
help.keys.action.undo: Undo the last change (not in text fields or forms)
help.keys.action.rail: Collapse or expand the sidebar (not in text fields)
help.keys.action.present: End the presentation; every what-if is discarded
help.cal.title: Calendar keyboard
help.cal.caption: Keys in the calendar
help.cal.action.arrows: Move to another day: left and right by one day, up and down by one week
help.cal.action.homeEnd: Go to the Monday or the Sunday of the week
help.cal.action.page: Go to the previous or next month
help.cal.action.enter: Select the day and show its details
help.ics.outlook.title: Classic Outlook
help.ics.outlook.3: Choose Import an iCalendar (.ics) or vCalendar file, then select the file.
help.ics.outlook.4: Choose Import to add the items to your calendar.
help.ics.newOutlook.title: New Outlook and Outlook on the web
help.ics.newOutlook.2: Choose Add calendar, then Upload from file.
help.ics.newOutlook.3: Select the .ics file and the calendar to add it to.
help.ics.google.title: Google Calendar
help.ics.google.3: Select the .ics file and the calendar to add it to.
help.ics.apple.title: Apple Calendar
help.ics.apple.3: Choose the calendar to add the events to.
help.ics.note: After a change, export again and import the new file the same way. Every entry keeps its ID and gets a newer version, so calendar apps that support updates replace the old entries instead of adding copies. Meetings that are gone since the last export of the same selection in this browser are included as cancelled. Not every app applies updates from a file; if you see entries twice, delete the old ones and import again.
help.keyboard.title: Keyboard
help.keyboard.intro: Caldence can be used with the keyboard alone. In the list of views, the arrow keys, Home and End switch between views.
help.keyboard.areas: While the upper level is selected, {structure} and {overview} are two buttons: Tab reaches them, Enter or Space switches the page. On the page {structure}, every person is a button: Enter or Space opens their card, and Escape closes it and returns to the person.
help.cal.action.escape: In the day details: close them
help.a11y.title: Accessibility
help.a11y.text: Caldence is built to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA in German and English, in light and dark mode. Every view works with the keyboard and is built for screen readers. The accessibility statement describes how this was tested and lists known limitations.
